correctness.rationale: Whitening the sampling covariance reduces the repeated-sampling ellipsoid statistic to Q equal to the sum of independent chi-square-one variables weighted by a_i=1/(1+lambda_i). Continuity gives a unique fixed-level ellipsoid scalar. Pathwise comparison with a_min times chi-square-d and a_max times chi-square-d gives strict interior bounds under anisotropy. For a contrast, the posterior-to-sampling variance ratio is a generalized Rayleigh quotient, whose worst direction yields tau_L=a_max. Finally Q dominates a_max times one chi-square-one term and is bounded above by a_max chi-square-d, while the upper quantiles of chi-square-one and chi-square-d have ratio tending to one, proving tau_E tends to tau_L. Fresh deterministic quadrature reproduced the package's two-dimensional value 0.6917708844598199.

final_claim: Under the stated bMGP Gaussian limits, scalar radial rescaling has an exact joint-ellipsoid calibration factor equal to a weighted-chi-square quantile ratio; under anisotropic covariance mismatch this factor lies strictly below the sharp scalar threshold required to avoid undercoverage in every linear contrast, and the two thresholds coalesce as confidence tends to one.
limitations: Asymptotic Gaussian calibration only; covariance-estimation error and finite-sample coverage are not analyzed.
